items.title: Four equivalent descriptions of a relatively very ample invertible sheaf for a quasi-compact morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four equivalent formulations of relative very ampleness for an invertible sheaf on a quasi-compact morphism: the definition, its being local on the base, an explicit graded algebra presentation with an immersion into a relative Proj, and the classical condition on the canonical map from the pullback of the pushforward being surjective with the associated morphism an immersion (statement lines 9145-9169). The counted proof has real content in two places: the passage from the local condition to the global one, where separatedness and adjunction produce surjectivity of the canonical map, and the verification that the associated morphism is an immersion by factoring it through an open subscheme of the projective bundle of the pushforward; the cycle is then closed by presenting a relative Proj as a closed subscheme of a projective bundle (proof lines 9165-9237). It is H2: the implications are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard projective bundle and relative Proj statements.
